name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,424

clue.text: Cut short promotion about game

indicators.note: one thing placed about another wraps around it, so the promotion surrounds the game

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, promotes a product
the card game

explanation.surface: A promotion campaign is curtailed because of some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' looks like it might trim a word, but it is the definition; 'about' wraps the promotion around the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged book or speech has been shortened by trimming material, so it was cut short.

clue.text: Lady scratching bottom attracted prince

indicators.note: scratching means removing, and the bottom of a down word is its final letter

blocks.note: a woman's name
drew in, attracted

explanation.surface: A woman with an itch catches a prince's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, which is what gets scratched off.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is the name of a British royal, a son of Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Turn back on green

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone turns around on a village green or golf green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn back' feels like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to return to a former state or go back.

clue.text: Abandon one leaving for upper-class wife

indicators.note: one letter leaving to make way for another means a swap of letters

blocks.note: to ditch is to abandon
Roman numeral one
U is the abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: An aristocrat replacing an abandoned spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In DITCH the I is replaced by U. 'Old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, from 'Duchess of Fife'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a man's Dutch, short for Duchess of Fife, is his spouse.

clue.text: Abstract example

blocks.note: first meaning: a summary of a text
second meaning: a perfect instance or embodiment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract' looks like an adjective modifying example but is a noun meaning a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome can be a condensed summary of a work, or the ideal typical instance of something.

clue.text: Outwardly feel compassion over dump

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside of the word, so only its two end letters are kept
turned over, the following word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: first and last letters of feel
compassion is pity

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry for a rubbish tip, or for a person at a dump.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly-tip is British slang for dumping waste illegally; 'dump' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly-tip is to discard rubbish illegally on open land, a specific kind of dumping.

clue.text: Presumably second storage facility that is for Scottish town

blocks.note: if the first locker is locker A, the second would be locker B
i.e., id est, that is

explanation.surface: A self-storage firm's second warehouse is meant for a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' signals the playful logic of lettered lockers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockerbie is a small town in Dumfries and Galloway, in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Pamphlet - one about medical procedure

blocks.note: a tract is a short pamphlet
Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A leaflet about a hospital operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but just gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the therapeutic pulling of a limb or spine with weights to treat injury.

clue.text: Rule out contralto appearing in first movement

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so the voice abbreviation goes within the movement

blocks.note: first part of the prelude, split around the insertion
C is the abbreviation for contralto
a prelude is an opening movement; its last four letters

explanation.surface: A conductor bars a contralto from singing in the opening movement.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside PRELUDE, the opening movement of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it from happening, making it impossible.

clue.text: Joint doctor violated

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical practitioner has broken the rules together with an accomplice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a carpentry joint of interlocking wedge-shaped tenons and slots.

clue.text: Get rid of last of the pickle

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter only of the word that follows

blocks.note: to scrap something is to discard it
final letter of the

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw away the remains of a jar of pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like food to be thrown out, but it means a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an awkward predicament or difficult situation someone has got into.

clue.text: Issue of Time to support old record company

blocks.note: EMI was a famous British record label
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An issue of Time magazine sponsored by a record label.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue T supports EMI by sitting beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, so to issue a sound or substance.

clue.text: Cook or warm the fisherman's bait?

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice on whether to cook or just heat an angler's bait.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the absurdity of cooking bait; 'the' is part of the fodder, not just filler.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers commonly thread worms dug from the soil onto hooks to attract fish.

clue.text: Praise extra tax cut

indicators.note: something cut has lost a piece, here the end of the tax word

blocks.note: the prefix ex- carries the sense of outside or beyond, as extra does
a toll is a levy or tax

explanation.surface: Applauding a reduction in an additional levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims only the tax word, by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify someone enthusiastically, which is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Desire contents of sugar container?

indicators.note: the contents of a container are what lies inside, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: a sachet holds a portion of sugar; drop its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Craving whatever is in the sugar bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The sugar container is a SACHET, and its inside is ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for or yearn for it intensely.

clue.text: Discards harpoon held by cheat - quite the reverse

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the answer is gripped inside the run of words
this flips the stated relation: the cheat is the thing held, not the thing holding

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A con artist hides a harpoon and throws away cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' flips the surface: the cheat is held by the words, not the harpoon by the cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins at card games by trickery.

clue.text: See means of identification on cigarette paper

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another comes after it, so the earlier pieces are placed behind the cigarette

blocks.note: tab is British slang for a cigarette
lo is an old word meaning look or see
ID, an identity document

explanation.surface: Instructions to check the ID written on a cigarette paper.
explanation.walkthrough: TAB is British slang for a cigarette, and LO is an old word for look; 'paper' is a newspaper, not the cigarette paper the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper of small page format, so a type of paper.

clue.text: Behind objection to tips in clinical knowledge summaries

indicators.note: the tips of words are their leading ends, so only the initials of the following phrase are kept

blocks.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
taken as written
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone lags behind in objecting to advice in medical guidance notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind is an informal noun for the rump, the part of the body one sits on.

clue.text: Parisian is international friend to value

blocks.note: est is French for is
I is the abbreviation for international
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is a worldwide companion worth valuing.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to appraise or judge the worth of something approximately.

clue.text: Open one's mouth

blocks.note: un is dialect for one, plus the S
trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: A plea to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as speaking up, but 'Open' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstrap a bag or buckle is to undo its fastenings, opening it.

clue.text: Reportedly break feet

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a pause is a break

explanation.surface: A report that someone broke their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Paws are the clawed or padded feet of animals such as cats and dogs.

clue.text: River follows westward pasture

definitions.note: verb: to put out to graze

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means reading from right to left, backwards

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
f is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: A river running west past a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To pasture livestock is to let them graze, that is to feed on grass.

clue.text: Knox, for example, organised computer language

blocks.note: Fort Knox, the US gold depository
ran, as in ran or managed an event

explanation.surface: Someone named Knox put together a programming language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal but means RAN; Knox is Fort Knox, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortran is an early high-level programming language used for scientific computation.

clue.text: Lovelessly leave out examination of a heart valve

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so without love means each word loses its round letter

blocks.note: to omit is to leave out
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Someone heartlessly skips a cardiac test.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, removed from both OMIT and ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The mitral valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle; the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Substantial dish in Cyprus

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: CY is the vehicle code for Cyprus; its first letter
a dish is an attractive person, a hunk
second letter of CY

explanation.surface: A hearty meal served on Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is not food but an attractive man, a HUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chunky means thick, solid and bulky, so large and substantial in size.

clue.text: Sets off for travels

blocks.note: first meaning: triggers, as an alarm or switch
second meaning: journeys or excursions

explanation.surface: Someone departs on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets off' looks like setting out on a journey; it means triggers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip activates a mechanism such as a circuit breaker, and trips are short journeys or excursions.

clue.text: Promise quiet entertaining Cambridge University author

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the quiet word holds the university

blocks.note: giving your word is promising
sh is the call for quiet
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A writer pledges to keep quiet while hosting a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University is not the English one here but MIT, in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsmith is a skilled writer, someone who crafts language for a living.

clue.text: Make a zig-zag movement to capture king for rook

indicators.note: one thing in place of another means a single letter is swapped

blocks.note: to snare is to capture
K is king in chess notation
R is rook in chess notation

explanation.surface: Chess advice: zig-zag to take the king with a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: In SNARE the R is replaced by K.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to wind or twist along a path, moving in curves like a serpent.

clue.text: Artist holds bible in court in Ascot?

indicators.note: a word that holds another has it inside, so the artist encloses the bible
in places the preceding pieces inside the court abbreviation

blocks.note: CT, the abbreviation for court, splits around the rest; its first letter
RA, Royal Academician, splits around the bible; its first letter
AV, the Authorised Version of the Bible
second letter of RA
second letter of CT

explanation.surface: A painter carries a bible into court at the Ascot races.
explanation.walkthrough: RA holds AV to make RAVA, which goes inside CT. An ascot is a broad neck scarf; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide formal neckerchief, a kind of cravat, named after the racecourse.

clue.text: Suffering leak in experiment

blocks.note: a trial is a painful ordeal
to run is to leak or flow, as colours run

explanation.surface: A drip causes distress during a scientific test.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a test or rehearsal carried out before the real thing.

clue.text: Searches for cleaners

blocks.note: first meaning: thorough searches
second meaning: chimney cleaners

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: Police make sweeps of an area when looking for something, and chimney sweeps clean flues.

clue.text: Make light of Penny leaving to get floor covering

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter is taken out of the phrase

blocks.note: to underplay is to make light of
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a coin's departure to buy a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERPLAY without its P gives UNDERLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlay is the cushioning material laid beneath a carpet over floorboards.
